paragraphs: The 316i has been a mainstay of the 3 Series diesel range since 2012, spanning two generations under one badge. Early F30/F31 models from 2012 to 2015 use the N47, a 2.0-litre diesel that's part of a family known for a specific timing chain issue. From late 2015 onwards, across both the F30/F31 and later the F30/F31, the 316i switched to the B47, a newer, significantly more reliable unit that doesn't share the N47's timing chain concerns. Knowing which one your car has matters, because the components and the known wear pattern differ - which is exactly why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting.
about.boldParagraph: The 316i is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: A 1.6-litre turbocharged four-cylinder fitted to the early F30/F31 316i. Known for timing chain guide wear over time — see the callout above. We replace the timing chain, guides and tensioners as standard on every N20 rebuild.

The later 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder, fitted from 2015. Generally reliable, with no specific widespread issue confirmed for the 316i application. We service it to the same standard as the N20.

compatibility.intro: Because the 316i spans two distinct engines within one generation, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an N20 part will work on a B48 car — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (N20 or B48) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic 316i quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
